lens.name: Data Story
lens.brief: A good dataset is a story with the narrator removed. Pick a public dataset that has something to say right now, such as game logs, weather, transit, space, population or prices, hand-simplify and bundle a snapshot, and tell the story through interaction. State the date and source of every number.
sourceHints: r/dataisbeautiful top of the month
Public NHL stats pages, NOAA, NASA open data, Our World in Data style public datasets
Wikipedia tables with CC licenses
data.gov-style open data portals

lens.name: Deckbuilder Systems Lab
lens.brief: Deckbuilders hide a probability engine: thinning, draw odds, synergy graphs, the quiet tyranny of a bad starter card. Build the instrument panel the genre never shipped: simulate ten thousand runs of a tiny invented deck and show which choices actually mattered.
sourceHints: r/slaythespire, r/balatro and r/roguelikes strategy threads
r/gamedev and itch.io deckbuilder jam postmortems
Wikipedia: Hypergeometric distribution, Monte Carlo method
r/boardgames design discussions on engine building

lens.name: Anti-Lens: The Opposite
lens.brief: Write down the most obvious idea for any topic of the day, then build its exact opposite. A calculator that refuses to give answers, a game about losing well, a map of nowhere, a visualization that hides data on purpose. It must still be good: opposites are a method, not an excuse.
sourceHints: Any hot thread, inverted
Wikipedia: Oblique Strategies, Reverse psychology, Negative space
r/InternetIsBeautiful top posts, then flip the premise
Are.na channels on anti-design

lens.name: Gloriously Overengineered
lens.brief: Solve a trivial problem with a ludicrous pipeline: forty configurable steps to pick a lunch, a distributed consensus protocol for choosing a movie. Every stage must actually do something, and the final answer should be correct enough to be annoying.
sourceHints: r/ProgrammerHumor and r/programming 'overengineering' threads
Wikipedia: Rube Goldberg machine, Consensus (computer science)
Hacker News Show HN: ridiculous solutions
r/Damnthatsinteresting machines

lens.name: Cartography Corner
lens.brief: Maps are arguments. Build a map toy where the projection, the scale or the data tells a story: distort a country by population, draw the isochrone of an old railway, compare where daylight falls on one date. Hand-simplify and bundle geometry; no tile services.
sourceHints: r/MapPorn, r/geography and r/dataisbeautiful maps
Wikipedia: Map projection, Cartogram, Natural Earth data
Natural Earth public-domain data
Hacker News cartography posts

lens.name: Jam Watch
lens.brief: Game jams put a theme on the table and let thousands of people interpret it. Pick the theme that is live this week and interpret it better than the average entry: a complete tiny game with a real mechanic, juicy feedback, and an ending. Credit the theme, not any particular entry.
sourceHints: itch.io jams calendar and featured jams
Ludum Dare and other open jam theme announcements
r/gamedev jam threads, r/WebGames
r/incremental_games

lens.name: Everyone's Toy
lens.brief: Make accessibility the creative engine rather than a checklist: a visual toy that is fully playable by ear, a color tool built for every kind of vision, a game that works with one switch. The inclusive version should be the best version, not the compromise.
sourceHints: r/accessibility, r/blind, r/deaf and r/gamedev accessibility threads
Wikipedia: Sonification, Color blindness, Universal design
Game Accessibility Guidelines (public)
Hacker News accessibility threads

lens.name: Mundane Epic
lens.brief: Take an everyday chore and score it like an epic quest: laundry as a siege, commuting as a roguelike, an inbox as a hydra. Real progression, real stakes, honest jokes about modern life. The best versions end up quietly useful.
sourceHints: r/CasualConversation and r/mildlyinteresting for everyday texture
r/incremental_games and r/roguelikes for progression design
Wikipedia: Gamification, Hero's journey
itch.io 'life sim' jam entries
